text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.3; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.508

g.text:soa: THE ST IVES GROUP

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Barbara Hepworth

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: A British sculptor who began working in the 1940s, Hepworth made the work for which she is best known in the artist colony of St Ives in Cornwall, south west England, where she spent most of her working life, along with Ben Nicholson and others.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: She was also a contemporary of Henry Moore.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Hepworth worked in stone, wood and metal, as well as making working drawings.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Her sculptures were smooth, often oval forms, which sometimes have holes (or voids) through them.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The voids might be spanned by string or wire strung across in parallel lines or fanning out like spokes, as if to create some kind of tension in the object.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Hepworth favoured highly polished black or white marble, granite, wood or bronze.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The sculptures ranged from small table sized ones, for example three perfectly smooth elliptical forms on a shallow plinth all made of white marble, or an elongated bronze shape standing on its end, to medium sized plinth based works such as the stringed elliptical voids, to large outdoor sculptures that sat on the ground, on stone boulders, or bronze plinths.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Hepworth made several large scale public commissions and her work can be seen in London on the façade of John Lewis, a London department store, in various public parks, for example on Hampstead Heath and in Battersea Park, and towering over the piazza of the United Nations building in New York.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: In most cases these works feature an oval shape often with strings, either in stone or bronze.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: For the UN building she made a large oval flat shape with a small hole through it, reminiscent of a stone standing on its end, which is placed next to an ornamental water feature.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The standing stones and other Stone Age monuments and monoliths that are common in Cornwall were part of her inspiration and Hepworth wanted her sculptures to sit in the landscape in the same way.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Ben Nicholson

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Nicholson was a leading member of the St Ives group and a contemporary of Barbara Hepworth who pioneered a style of work that is a cross between constructivism and geometric abstraction.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: His paintings often have raised areas made by shapes cut from plywood.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He used white and grey and added lines and smaller areas of brighter colours.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He also made representational works, most of which feature the Cornish land and seascapes.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Winifred Nicholson

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: St Ives painter.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Terry Frost

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: A younger British artist who was a member of the St Ives group in the 1950s and 60s.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Frost made abstract pattern paintings, using irregular squashed circular shapes in a repeated pattern, in black and white with red, dark green, blue and other colours.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Sometimes the paintings would consist of a part of a large solid black circle on one side of the canvas, and a part of a red circle on the opposite side.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The clean lines, minimal forms, bright colours and black and white of Frost’s paintings were very in tune with contemporary fashion and design.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Naum Gabo

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: An eastern European artist who lived and worked in Britain, Gabo made sculptures and maquettes for proposed sculptures from wood, metal, acrylic, wire and thread.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Gabo’s formal abstract structures have a strong architectural element in their reliance on apparent tension and cantilevering for their structural strength.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: They are clearly influenced by Russian constructivism and Suprematism, but they also relate to the sculptural forms of Barbara Hepworth, in which voids and solid form are often given tension by thread or wires stretched across in parallel lines.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Most of his work is very small, around 40 cm high.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Gabo’s use of very new materials and his architectural forms made him unique in his time, and he developed a body of work that is singular in its devotion to an aesthetic and to material.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He also made preparatory drawings and sketches.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Peter Lanyon

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: A St Ives painter who painted semi abstract landscapes using a lot of green, brown and white.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Alfred Wallis

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Walllis painted the harbours, fishing boats and the sea around St Ives, often using an eccentric perspective that combined aerial and frontal views.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.3; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.508

g.text:soa: THE COBRA GROUP

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: This was a group of artists working in Holland who made semi abstract paintings during the 1940s and 50s.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Karel Appel

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Appel was the leader of the CoBRA group.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: His paintings of figures with smiling toothy faces are made with bright colours and lots of impasto.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.3; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.508

g.text:soa: ABSTRACTION

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Malevich and Kandinsky had given the fullest expression to early abstraction.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: By the 1940s abstraction was developing fast both in Europe and most particularly in America.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Many painters who had begun their careers painting figuratively turned to abstraction, de Kooning being one example.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Some made works that were minimal in style, others worked towards abstract expressionism.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Willem de Kooning

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: An American artist who worked from the 1950s to the 1990s, de Kooning made paintings in a great variety of styles, from figurative to abstract.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He is best known for two periods of his work, the first made in the 1950s and consisting of a series of small portraits of women grinning with lots of teeth, painted in an almost impossibly thick and encrusted impasto, the surface of the canvas heavy with blobs of multi coloured paint that project from its surface producing an overall brown colour in combination.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Like Rothko, de Kooning did not subscribe to the notion of the artist as knowing subject but to the Kantian idea of pure art.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: De Kooning’s second well known group of works are the controversial late paintings, made after the artist was diagnosed with Alzheimer’s disease.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: These are very large paintings made with thin bright primary colours of paint applied in single brush strokes that barely cover the white primed surface of the canvas giving the impression of a white painting roughly covered in gestural marks.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Some critics considered them to be an extraordinary late flowering, others that they were inconsequential in de Kooning's oeuvre due to his mental state.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: De Kooning is vilified by American artist Paul McCarthy in a film in which McCarthy appears dressed as a paint tube, squirting paint everywhere and chanting ‘de Kooning, de Kooning’ in an infantile way.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Josef Albers

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: An American painter born around 1900, Albers made geometric abstractions usually based on the square, using dull versions of primary colours.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He was interested in the optical effects of colours on each other.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Albers was a lifelong teacher of art and as is discussed in Eva Hesse’s posthumously published diary as her professor.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Yves Tanguy

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Tanguy was a French artist who made semi abstract paintings showing organic sculptural forms.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Tanguy also made kinetic sculptures (the best known of which is in Paris outside the Centre Pompidou) consisting of similar forms that were constructed so that they would be animated by cause and effect, such as wind moving a vane, or water flow.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Every movement of the sculpture creates sounds.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Ad Reinhardt

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: An American artist who made minimal abstract paintings, mostly in grey and black, from the 1960s to 80s.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Clyfford Still

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Still’s abstract paintings often have large areas of flat colour to which he adds a contrasting area, the rough edge of which encroaches on the predominant colour.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Antoni Tapies

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: A Spanish painter who made abstract paintings that resemble doors and walls.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Tapies used textural materials and built up the surface of his canvas to create paintings that are almost reliefs, in predominantly natural colours such as dark brown, black and white.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Robert Ryman

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Ryman is known as the white on white painter; he only used white paint (although he often used a bright coloured ground).

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Ryman’s paintings are mostly small, they are neatly made but with quite thick paint and lots of blobs and brushstrokes.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Robert Motherwell

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: An American abstract expressionist painter who made very big paintings often using a lot of black paint applied with large brushes and leaving other areas as bare canvas.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Leon Golub

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: American artist born in the 1930s who made abstract paintings.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Elizabeth Murray

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: An American artist who made wall reliefs and constructions that she called three dimensional paintings.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Victor Pasmore

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: British artist who made abstract paintings and works on paper.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Eileen Agar

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: A British artist who made sculptures and reliefs, both abstract and symbolist, as well as some small objects.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Mel Bochner

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Bochner’s characteristic works are dull coloured semi abstract cityscapes in a geometric hard edged style.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Morris Louis

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Louis is an American artist who is known for his abstract pour paintings made in the 1960s and 70s.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Louis developed a technique for pouring paint onto raw canvas and allowing the paint to pool and spread, soaking into the canvas yet allowing the colours to remain distinct from one another.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The resulting works usually consist of brightly coloured stripes emanating from one side of the canvas, spreading and blending on the edges, with the texture of the surface of the canvas always visible.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Frank Stella

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: An American artist who made wall drawings and reliefs, which consisted of painted cut outs arranged as an abstract assemblage on a panel fixed to the wall.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Lucio Fontana

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The Italian artist Fontana’s paintings from the 1950s and 60s are abstract, plain and flat coloured canvases with slits cut right through the canvas.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Sometimes Fontana added some textural detail, such as painted gravel or wool thread.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He used a range of colours from dark reds and blues to bright copper green.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Sometimes his paintings are made on egg shaped canvases.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Mary Heilman

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: An abstract painter born in the 1940s, Heilman makes small paintings of carefully considered abstract shapes, lines and forms exploring endless possibilities of form and colour.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Al Held

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Twentieth century American painter.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Howard Hodgkin

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Hodgkin is a British painter born in the 1940s who makes abstract paintings.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He uses very bright jewel like colours, applied in large, often round, repeated splodges, the paint continuing right off the edge of the canvas onto and round the frame.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Hodgkin’s paintings are never larger than 2 metres high.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He sometimes uses round and oval shaped canvases.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Hodgkin has made work for public commission including a large photomural of brushstrokes that fills the circular facade of an Imax cinema in London.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Bridget Riley

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Riley is famous for her Op Art black and white paintings made in the 1960s, work which endures as one of the most recognisable images of the 1960s.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: She made these paintings by drawing and distorting grids and filling them in with black and white.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The distortions create illusions of curves, of shimmering and of motion making the paintings hard to look at.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Riley used grids of squares, triangles, as well as dots and ellipses and parallel lines.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: One painting, one metre high, has a grid of squares that gradually decrease in width as they move toward the centre of the painting, creating the illusion of two vertical chequered cylinders.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Another painting, one and a half metres by two metres, has parallel horizontal wavy lines, each line fractionally further to one side of the painting than the next, creating an optical shimmer.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: A large, two metre square painting has black elliptical dots placed about 30 cm apart on a grid, the angle of each ellipse changing gradually, giving an impression of motion.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: A triangle pattern creates waves as each of the triangles on the square canvas is progressively tilted along a curved line.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Riley made a large number of black and white works before beginning to add one or two colours, for example yellow, red and blue, to the black and white paintings.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: A horizontal wavy line painting has colour added.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: In the 1980s Riley began to explore the optical colour blending effects she had created, and made the first of a large number of pure colour works.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: She ceased to use black and white and has never returned to it.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: She continued to study the work of Cézanne and to refer to his paintings in her geometric abstractions, many of which draw directly on historical painting.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Works from this period are mostly a grid of multicoloured parallelograms, the choice of colour influenced by the source image.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: These images predate but later seemed to anticipate pixellation.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Riley has made many public commissions including applying bands of coloured stripes to the corridors on several floors of a London hospital.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: During the late 1990s and early 2000s Riley continued to use colour but began to draw much larger shapes.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The shapes in her paintings remain hard edged but she ceased to use a grid.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The tendencies evident in early twentieth century abstract painting developed into two distinct but complementary movements, abstract expressionism and minimalism.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.3; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.508

g.text:soa: ABSTRACT EXPRESSIONISM

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The critic Clement Greenberg argued for Abstract Expressionism as the only logical way forward for painting.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He supported many of its best exponents, including Pollock.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Jackson Pollock

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The best known of the American abstract expressionist painters and arguably the best known modernist painter of all time.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Pollock was born in the 1920s and died in the early 70s in a car accident.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Pollock began working in the 1950s and at the end of the decade he started to experiment, placing the canvas on the floor and using a brush to pour house paint, not touching the canvas at all.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: This was a radical step, since no one had ever made a painting without touching the canvas and with so little control over the result.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Pollock’s drip paintings caused a sensation.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: His new method became known as action painting.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The photographer Hans Namuth made a seminal film of Pollock showing him pouring paint on the canvas, which included a section filmed from below through glass.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The action paintings are up to 2 metres high and very wide and are all composed of an all over ‘pattern’ of drips, applied in a dynamic but highly controlled way, so that a design is evident.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Far from relinquishing control, Pollock became master of the technique.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The combinations of colours are subtle, usually involving black and white with one or two other colours.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: One of the best known is Blue Poles, which has two vertical blue stripes amidst the swirling drips.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Another, titled One, is a largely black and white composition.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Pollock made many public commissions and his work was taken up by the American government as representing the pinnacle of modernist achievement in art.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: His work was seen as symbolising the freedom of the American way of life.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Unwittingly Pollock’s work was used as US propaganda against the Soviet Union, when the CIA covertly funded an international touring exhibition of the work of the abstract expressionists designed to be compared directly and unfavourably with soviet socialist realist art.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Pollock was married to Lee Krasner, also an abstract painter.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Krasner saw Pollock through many years of increasing alcoholism and infidelity, taking him to live and work in a house on Long Island to help him stop drinking, until she felt compelled to leave him although she continued to care for him.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Krasner subjugated her own career to Pollock’s and it seems reasonable to suppose that he was unlikely to have become successful, or to have even made the action paintings, without her support.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Susan Rothenstein

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: American abstract expressionist painter.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Franz Kline

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: American Kline’s enormous abstract expressionist paintings usually feature large black gestural marks made with a big brush on a white, or even un primed ground.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Much of the ground is left untouched but it becomes an active part of the surface of the painting.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Lee Krasner

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: American figurative painter who turned to abstraction.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: She established a foundation in her own and her husband Jackson Pollock’s names, which through its grant making activities contributes to the careers of many artists.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Helen Frankenthaler

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: American abstract expressionist painter.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Barnett Newman

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: American painter Newman’s minimal paintings are known for ‘the zip’, a line of a contrasting colour running vertically down the canvas.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Newman invariably used one or two solid colours in blocks or bands, often dark blue, black and maroon, but also golden ochre colours and aquamarine, and the zip (red on a dark brown ground for example) animated these, setting up an optical resonance.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He spent his whole career painting these and like Rothko was held up as a spiritual painter.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: One group of paintings on a single theme fills a whole room; they are white on white paintings with elements of black.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Mark Rothko

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Rothko is an American painter who is one of the most famous exponents of abstract expressionism.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Rothko’s works are simple colour fields, predominantly one or two shades of the same colour or two contrasting colours, often arranged as a wide border with a central section and usually in portrait format.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Although the colour is solid, it is roughly painted with an uneven edge so that the colours affect each other optically.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Rothko’s paintings are quite large, up to 3 metres high and he sometimes made four works to be shown together.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: One such installation is a dark red group of paintings consisting of blurred rectangles within borders.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: This installation provokes a spiritual or contemplative response in many viewers, some of whom say they are moved to tears.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: These works are often used as exemplification that art can provide a transcendental experience.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Rothko referred to his paintings as parts of himself, describing them as skins hung on the wall.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.3; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.508

g.text:soa: MINIMALISM

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: In the late 1950s and early 60s minimalism was an emerging trend in both painting and sculpture.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Minimalist sculpture was groundbreaking in it refusal of any form of modelling, and in its use of prefabricated materials.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Robert Morris

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: An American sculptor who was known for his use of fabricated steel and other metals.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Morris made abstract minimal sculptures, which were nearly always cube shapes, about one and a half meters high, open at the top.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: His series of copper plated boxes shown as a group are particularly well known, as well as a similar series made of mirrored glass.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The copper boxes emit a glowing pink reflected light from their interiors.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: These are contradictory works in terms of their representation of a heavy solid mass by means of emptiness and light.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Morris also made sculpture with pieces of heavyweight felt that he scattered on the floor.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He collaborated in a live performance with Carolee Schneeman in the 1970s titled Olympia.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Richard Serra

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: An American artist who is well known for his monumental sculpture in steel, Titled Arc, which was installed in a public plaza in the 1980s.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Tilted Arc was a curving steel wall that bisected the plaza and was tilted at a steep angle along its length.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: It became notorious for the degree of public resistance to it (the sculpture created a detour making the walk across the square longer), and for the fact that a worker was killed when a part of the sculpture fell on him during installation.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Serrra’s work consisted of mostly welded steel sculpture, but not always on such a scale.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: An early video work, Hand Catching Lead, shows the sculptor’s hand trying repeatedly to catch a piece of falling lead, a difficult task which is rarely successful.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Donald Judd

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: American Donald Judd is one of the most important of the minimal sculptors.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He made steel boxes, shelf like structures and repeated units, fabricated with a high attention to detail and immaculately spray painted in a variety of colours.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Some sculptures are made of polished metal such as brass, so that they are extremely shiny.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The structures and units are ambiguous, suggesting function but obviously non functional.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: They are either mounted on the wall, in a horizontal line or one above the other, sometimes in ascending sizes, or placed with precision on the floor.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The I Beam is one of Judd’s favourite materials; he pioneered the use of pre fabricated steel and modular construction in his sculptures creating simple works that often had a monumental quality.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Judd set up a studio and a foundation in Marfa, Texas.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Carl Andre

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Andre is another of the leading artists in the generation of American minimalist sculptors that includes Judd and Morris.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He is notorious for his ‘pile of bricks’, purchased by the Tate gallery in London in 1980, which was derided in the press for being nothing but a pile of ordinary house bricks.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: This work, an arrangement of house bricks to form a plinth two bricks thick, was similar to his other works, chiefly floor works consisting of metal tiles arranged in rectangles and lines.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: It was important for the viewer’s experience of the work that they were free to walk on the sculpture.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: These works are both self effacing in their near invisibility and grandiose in their ambition.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Andre said that they represented footprints of much larger structures.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He wanted to imply monolithic structures through minimal and economic means, creating a tension between the monolithic and the invisible.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Andre also made a number of text works, some with ‘x’s and ‘o’s typed in rows, and others consisting of concrete poetry made by fitting words into some kind of geometric system.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Brice Marden

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: American painter of minimal abstract works who made large (often at least 2 by 3 metre) canvases which are painted in muted colours, often grey with one or two contrasting coloured stripes on the edge of the canvas.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Marden's work has similar formal qualities to the work of Barnett Newman, although where Newman's work is painterly, Marden’s is hard edged and painted with flat solid colour.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Agnes Martin

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Martin’s minimal abstract paintings are usually based on a grid and they are mainly white with pencil thin lines of bright colours.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The detail of the painting is barely perceptible from a distance; they are cool, calm and full of light, and rigorous in their execution.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: John McCracken

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: A British artist who makes minimal abstract sculptures in the form of planks and cubes with a high gloss lacquered finish in solid colours.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The planks (about 3 metres long, 50 cm wide and 10 cm deep) typically lean against the gallery wall, while other sculptures are hung from the wall.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Yvonne Rainer

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: An American choreographer who worked with artists such as Robert Rauschenberg and Jasper Johns, as well as musicians such as John Cage on collaborative performance works, for example The Mind is a Muscle, made in 1971.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: These works were developed largely at the Black Mountain College summer school and at the Judson Church Centre in New York and were unusual in their day for being multidisciplinary.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Rainer choreographed dance works based on the repetition of everyday movements eschewing classical dance form and skills.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: This emphasis on the everyday had its parallels in both minimalism and Pop Art.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Rainer later went on to become a filmmaker and in the 1990s made her first feature film.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.3; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.508

g.text:soa: TOWARDS POP ART

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Artists such as Rauschenberg, Johns and Lichtenstein took the logic of abstraction and minimalism and applied it to everyday objects and images.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Their innovations paved the way for pop art.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Robert Rauschenberg

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Rauschenberg began his career in the late 1950s and was part of New York pop art in the 60s.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He worked in all media and is particularly known for his paintings to which objects are attached.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The object would be made part of the painting or in some cases a painting be made part of a sculpture by extending the paint from canvas to object.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Rauschenberg’s innovation was to use screen printing as a medium, transferring images onto his canvases even before Warhol did, in particular photographic images from newspapers, cityscapes and street signs, before adding paint and even found objects.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: One of his best known paintings features a multi layered image of a city with a stop sign, a sign that reads ‘one way’ and architectural elements and abstract areas of colour.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Another has a photographic transfer of President Kennedy.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Rauschenberg made many works from found images and objects.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: One painting features a wooden chair attached to the canvas, and in another a single mattress with sheets, pillow and blankets becomes the canvas and is hung on the wall and painted on.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Rauschenberg's conceptual painterly abstraction was important in the early development of pop art.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He also made many drawings, including notably one called ‘Erased de Kooning’, which was simply that: a drawing by de Kooning erased by Rauschenberg.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Rauschenberg worked with Merce Cunningham, the dancer and member of the Judson Church collective of artist and dancers which including choreographer Yvonne Rainer, designing sets, lighting and costumes for dance performances.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He would often paint the set and the costumes himself.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: For one dance work he made a canvas backdrop painted with spots and matching spotted bodysuits for the dancers.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Jasper Johns

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: American artist born in the 1930s, Johns was one of the artists who made the move from figuration to abstraction in the 1950s, and then in the 1960s began to use recognisable symbols in his paintings, the best known being the American flag.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Johns and his contemporary Rauschenberg paved the way for Pop Art.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Johns’s target paintings use a circular target motif (the kind used for archery or shooting) of black and white, or red yellow and blue.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The paintings are portrait format so that the circular target is placed in the picture plane and there are sometimes other elements in the composition.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Johns’s American flag paintings were innovative for their use of a pre existing symbol to make an abstract image; they are simply painted American flags, the stars and stripes covering the canvas edge to edge.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: These paintings were also significant because at the time the American flag was being burnt by protesters against the Vietnam War.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Johns went on to make a proliferation of flag paintings, drawings and lithographs usually in red, white and blue.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Then he began changing the colours culminating in a series of black on black and white on white flags, and even an edition of bronze flag table sculptures.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Johns also made a series of number paintings, simply painting the numbers zero to nine, drawn using a stencil to fill a large canvas edge to edge.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: These were made in many versions including white on white.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The idea to make an ordinary object into an art object led Johns to make some bronze sculptures, the best known of which are the Beer Cans and the Can of Brushes.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: These life size replicas are painted in true to life colours.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Roy Lichtenstein

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Lichtenstein’s work is among the best known of the American pop artists.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He made paintings using images from printed cartoon magazines by taking single frames or even a detail from a frame and enlarging it, initially to about 1 metre high but eventually to a much larger size.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He then made a painting from the drawing, reproducing exactly what he saw including any text.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Initially the paintings were black and white but Lichtenstein soon moved to use colour.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The paintings nearly always feature a person, a part of a vehicle and a graphic or textual depiction of fire, speed or force; they are part of a larger narrative that we are left to guess at.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Eventually Lichtenstein began to paint the dots made by the printing process, the dots which are obvious on billboards when they are viewed close up.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: By making the dots part of the painting Lichtenstein was reproducing both the reproduction and the means of its reproduction and actually painting the printing process.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He used the cyan magenta and yellow process colours on a white ground with black.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Certain of Lichtenstein’s works are iconographic, for example one of a fighter pilot in a cockpit of a plane that has a yellow flash coming from the fuselage.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The text announces the pilot’s thoughts at that moment.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Another is of a glamorous woman crying, again with text revealing her thoughts.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: His style was, and still is, copied, plagiarised and borrowed.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.3; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.508

g.text:soa: POP ART

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Andy Warhol

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Warhol is one of the most significant artists of the late twentieth century.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He was born in the 1930s and began his career as a graphic designer in his twenties.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He was very accomplished at drawing and became an artist.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Warhol is best known for his Campbell’s Soup Can paintings and his Marilyn paintings, but these are only a small part of his extremely prolific output.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Warhol’s early graphic work included advertisements for shoe shops, clothes shops, children and adult book illustrations, book jackets and packaging.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He used pen and ink, colour and sometimes added gold leaf.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He began to make screen prints.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Warhol became an artist and turned his studio into a gathering place and workshop called The Factory.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He made his own work at The Factory but by virtue of his eccentric personality and arresting style began to gather around him a coterie of colleagues, assistants and admirers.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Warhol’s hair was bleached white and he was never seen without dark glasses on and in stylish clothes.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He was close to the most inspiring people in the fashion, music and art worlds.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: It is often said that Warhol himself and The Factory are productions of Warhol’s art; certainly Warhol’s persona was unique and The Factory was an unprecedented example of collaborative practice.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: At The Factory Warhol worked with photographer Billy Name, who documented everything that happened there, models such as Viva and Edie Sedgwick (among others), who were really his muses, actors and any young and beautiful people who interested him.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The force of Warhol’s personality and the mystique that he created around himself meant that people were very keen to work with him or to commission him to make a portrait.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Warhol was obsessed with fame.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Sedgwick and Viva starred in Chelsea Girls, Warhol’s only feature film.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Many other short experimental films were made at the factory including Empire State, a single static shot of the Empire State building 24 hours long, that documented the changing light on the building.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Warhol said he wanted to make a film that people could watch when they were stoned.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The Screen Tests are a series of head and shoulder shots of just about anyone who passed through the doors of the factory, including many who years later became well known, those who didn’t, and those who were well known at the time.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Warhol would simply ask the person to sit and look at the camera.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Warhol published a groundbreaking fashion, music and art magazine called Interview and made a series of television chat shows for which he interviewed people.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Underpinning all this activity was the continuous production of Warhol’s paintings.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Warhol took the most ordinary mass produced object and represented it as art, making a photographic silk screen of the label on a Campbell’s soup can.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He did this as an anti art gesture, believing like other pop artists that art did not need to have noble subject matter and that art was a commodity like any other.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: To this end he used images of coke bottles, Brillo pad boxes and cornflake boxes among others to make his paintings, repeating the colour images in rows to cover the canvas, robbing the image of its original meaning.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He produced these in multiples, denying them any exclusivity.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He also made sculptures of plywood replica Brillo boxes in the same way.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Warhol made a screen print from a photograph of Marilyn Monroe to which he added paint by hand on the lips, eyes and hair.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He made as many of these as he felt like, painting each one differently.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Multiples of the Marilyns, each one always the same size (1 metre high), are often hung in rows and blocks and they have become so famous as to be almost ubiquitous, exactly as Warhol would have wanted.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He was attracted to Monroe because of her fame and glamour and made a vast number of paintings of her including a pair of round canvases painted gold, with her image printed in black on one and the other left blank.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: As well as the Marilyns, Warhol made a large number of paintings of Chairman Mao in the same way.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He also made a number of images of an Electric Chair, again made in a wide variety of colour schemes, as well as a Last Supper, and repeated images of Jesus on one canvas.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: His very numerous portrait commissions, which were a mainstay of the Factory’s finances, included Jackie Onassis, Joan Collins, Elvis and many society and business figures.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Warhol also made a number of self portraits, including one with sticking up hair.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Towards the end of his life Warhol made some collaborative paintings with Jean Michel Basquiat.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He died in the 1980s.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Claes Oldenburg

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: This American artist is known for his soft sculptures that he began to make in the 1960s.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Along with Warhol, Oldenburg was the main pop art sculptor.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He worked in a number of different media and also made a large number of working drawings.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The soft sculptures are made of canvas or vinyl, sewn and stuffed in the manner of soft toys, and then painted.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The sculptures represent vastly enlarged objects such as a light switch made in white vinyl, a drum kit made in painted canvas and a hamburger.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Each are accurately scaled up and constructed, but stuffed loosely so that they sag and collapse.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The light switch (about one metre square) hangs drooping on the wall, the drum kit (3 metres across) flops in a heap on the floor.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Oldenburg also made many painted clay sculptures, roughly modelled and painted, some cast in bronze, of which one of a hamburger is the best known.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: In the 1970s Oldenburg began to make public sculpture and also made a large number of designs, plans and sketches for monumental works, which were not always realised.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: These include a 30 metre high lipstick monument, a building based on the head of Mickey Mouse and one based on an electrical plug.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Ed Ruscha

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Ruscha became well known in the late 1960s for his paintings of words.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Ruscha took the sign and the billboard as his inspiration and made the painted word the subject of his work; he is best known for his painting of the Hollywood sign.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Ruscha used a variety of typefaces and three dimensional letters in his work, and also made a series of paintings of words as substance, for example the word ‘oil’ painted to look like oil.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He also made landscape paintings to which words are added.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Sometimes Ruscha used a (literal or imaginary) diagonal line in his paintings that he attributes to the compositional elements in classical painting.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: James Rosenquist

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Rosenquist has made some of the largest paintings of any contemporary artist.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: As a pop artist he is distinguished by his skill for painting on a vast scale acquired during his years as a professional billboard painter, painting images on hoardings above Times Square in New York for example.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Rosenquist is known for two paintings in particular, made in 1961, both of which are 4 or 5 metres high and around 25 metres long.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: F111 shows an American military aircraft, the painted lady on its side, and various other military items alluding to the contemporary Vietnam War protest movement.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The other work shows a collage of items of Americana of varying relative sizes, such as hugely enlarged tinned spaghetti, celebrating the emerging consumer culture in tune with the spirit of the times.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Rosenquist’s paintings often include the image of an idealised woman.
