text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Rosenquist was a contemporary of Andy Warhol and shared much of the same subject matter, but the two artists were unaware of each other’s work until late in the 1960s.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Rosenquist continued to work on the same scale throughout his career refining his technique with new digital imaging technology to help it became very far removed from his original billboard style.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: In the late 1999s onwards, he made a return to the way he had worked in the 1960s.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Patrick Caulfield

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: On of the best British pop artists, Caulfield is known for his very distinctive hard edged representative paintings of domestic interiors.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He chose to paint interiors or elements from interiors such as furniture, lighting and ceramics, and developed a way of making paintings that he never deviated from.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Caulfield copies the most basic structure of a scene from a photograph, rendering the forms with the minimum of line possible.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He treats light and shadow as solid object and draws both in the same way so that the light from a table lamp will be represented as a solid yellow shape, the shadow behind its shade as a black shape.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: All the objects in a painting are given equal importance, since every element is treated the same.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The outlines are painted in flat acrylic using a schematic, dramatically simplified black outline with the objects, walls, floors, light fittings, furniture being filled in with bright colours.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: These black lines are vaguely reminiscent of the lead in a stained glass window, yet they also call to mind Matisse’s painting.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Caulfield had several favourite subjects, among them the lamp and the vase.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He made many small paintings each around 50 cm high of one or two items, as well as many of entire interiors on a larger scale usually 2 metres high or more.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: His paintings can be seventeenth century Dutch interiors and still lifes; he painted the aspirations of an equivalent social group in his own day.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Caulfield’s best known works are some of the simple still lifes, for example a single lamp, a goldfish in a bowl, an ashtray with a cigarette, a vase, an oval mirror which somehow conveys the idea that it is reflective even though it is painted in black and white.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The schematic, iconographic way these things are painted makes them deceptively simple to look at.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Of his larger works, perhaps the interiors of a Swiss bar, is the best known.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: This interior is painted mainly in blue (with the usual black outline), which signifies the quality of light in the place rather than the materials of which the furniture is made.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: In this work Caulfield uses trompe l’oeil, another characteristic technique: the photo mural on the wall behind the banquette seating is painted realistically in that it looks like a view of an actual mountain scenery rather than a schematic representation.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Another example in which Caulfield paints a piece of wood grain realistically makes the direct acknowledgment of Braque’s work more explicit.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Caulfield never painted a person.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Richard Hamilton

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Hamilton is another well known British pop artist who made paintings that are figurative and usually have a realistically painted element to them, perhaps a figure, combined with an abstract, more painterly element.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Parts of the paintings are often blurry and watery, painted on un primed or thinly primed canvas.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Like many of the pop artists, Hamilton used the techniques of graphic art, such as air brushing and photographic reproduction, in combination with oil painting.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: This can be seen in the painting of the IRA hunger striker Bobby Sands during the period of his dirty protest made in the 1970s which shows the long haired, bearded Sands in his prison cell in front of a wall smeared with his own excrement.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Hamilton used an airbrush to paint the excrement as blurry brown squiggles.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Hamilton’s collages are made as sketches for paintings but sometimes are presented as works in their own right, such as Hamilton’s arguably best known work, A Plan for Everyday Living.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: This shows a montage of a modern domestic interior, an apartment with cantilevered stairs descending into a double height living area with picture windows that are being vacuumed by a body builder dressed only in a frilly apron.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Eduardo Paolozzi

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Paolozzi is a British artist who made works on paper and sculpture that could be considered as pop art.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Paolozzi specialised in patterns based on a grid of small coloured squares, which are complex and highly decorative, referring both to historical architectural decoration and textile design as well as to 1960s graphic style.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He used the same patterning to create cast metal sculptures, often made from aluminium.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: In the 1980s Paolozzi was commissioned to design the mosaic tiling for the walls of Tottenham Court Road underground station in London.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: This commission made Paolozzi’s work one of the most frequently encountered public art commissions in the world.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Peter Blake

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: British pop artist who is known best for his the sleeve design of the Beatle’s Sergeant Pepper album.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Blake’s paintings are dense, detailed figurative collage style works.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: They often contain elements of patterning, decorative borders and are meticulously painted.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He often chose to portray British national identity in some way.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He included a self portrait in many paintings – he always appears with long hair and a long beard.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Jim Dine

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: A contemporary of Rauschenberg and Johns in New York in the 1960s, Dine's best known work features his trademark hearts, drawn in outline or painted often in red or pink on white.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Robert Longo

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Longo is an American artist who made paintings, drawings and sculptures in the 1970s and 80s.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The sculptures are usually complementary to, or even shown as a part of a painted work.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Longo made a number of works in two and a half metre high panels arranged in threes and fours, one panel showing a man clothed in a suit apparently falling to the ground (perhaps having been shot), although he could almost be dancing, the other panels blank white or with photographic cityscapes.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The pencil and graphite drawing on the panels is very realistic.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: In some cases there is a bronze cast of a similar male figure placed in front of the wall panels, the best known being of a man ‘falling’, the balance of the sculpture precarious.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Robert Indiana

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: A screen print and sculpture made by Indiana became the motif for a generation.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He placed the letters of the word ‘love’ one on top of the other to form a cube shape with a distinctive slanted letter ‘O’.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Pop art was a major movement in twentieth century modern art.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Conceptual art had been developing from its roots in dada and surrealism, notably in the work of European artists who had been influenced by these movements such as Klein and Broodthaers.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Yves Klein

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Although he cannot be classed purely as a conceptual artist, French artist Klein’s subject was the condition of art, and he made several works that gained him notoriety, in particular the Blue Paintings.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: These were made as a performance in a gallery in Paris.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Klein invited female models to act as human brushes.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He applied ultramarine blue paint to their naked bodies and then directed them to position themselves and move their bodies in certain ways, making body prints onto paper he had placed on the floor and walls.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Klein’s idea was to use the nude to paint the nude.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The resulting body prints were exhibited, but it is the photographic documentation of the event that has become better known.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Later on he made some paintings by setting fire to canvases, singeing them and marking them with smoke.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Ultramarine blue was Klein’s trademark colour that he used for all of his painted work and sculpture.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He made a large number of paintings in the 1950s and early 60s using natural sponges stuck to canvas and painted blue.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He also made simple plain blue canvases.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Similarly he made sculptures with the sponges, creating tableaux of his flower or seaweed like creations.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Klein worked briefly in ceramics, making small sculptures that drew on porcelain table ornaments, lumpen thrown together and glazed versions that nevertheless made their sources clear.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The other strand to Klein’s work is more conceptual.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He made many works with found objects and works that were events and documentations of actions.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He made a work with a light bulb and several works with furniture.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The best known of these works is Leap into the Void, a staged photograph in which Klein is seen apparently leaping off a high wall in a street and falling through the air.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: There is a house on the left and a lamp post behind him.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Paris Air is a sealed glass vial containing nothing but air, to which Klein accorded a status as an artwork and a monetary value.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: In a performance work Klein sold gold leaf which he had authenticated to collectors and then invited them to throw the work they had just bought into the river Seine.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He also printed his own bonds, and sold these as works of art.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The work that summed up Klein’s interests most completely was The Void, a staged event for which Klein rented an empty gallery.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He sent out invitations to the opening of his exhibition, provided champagne and hired a commissionaire to stand on the door.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: No one was allowed to enter the gallery without an invitation and when they did so they found an empty gallery – the void of the title.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Marcel Broodthaers

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Like Klein, the Belgian artist Marcel Broodthaers cannot be defined as a conceptual artist but he draws both from this and surrealism.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Broodthaers occupies an eccentric personal world that centres around his Musée des Aigles, and the mussel shell.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Broodthaers was something of a surrealist, with his use of puns and irony, and juxtaposition of unlikely objects.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He created his own, sometimes impenetrable, lexicon of signs and symbols, and indeed signs were part of his work.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He made pressed sheet metal signs displaying diagrammatic objects such as a pipe, with ‘fig 1’ and ‘fig 2’ written underneath.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He made a number of small sculptures and wall reliefs using mussel shells stuck together.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The Musée des Aigles (Museum of Eagles) contained things that the artist had collected which bore eagles' wings, such as military crests.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.3; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.508

g.text:soa: CONCEPTUAL ART

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Hans Haacke

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: American Haacke became one of the best known of the 1970s’ conceptual artists in America and Europe.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: His practise was political in the sense that his subject matter was a critique of multinational corporations and advertising.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Haacke made a number of installations consisting of text panels with photographs detailing the activities of multinational companies such as William Morris, often subverting advertising design used by the company.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Haacke's earlier sculptural work includes a piece called Condensation Cube (1965), a Plexiglas cube about 50 cm square with naturally occurring and accumulating droplets of condensation inside it.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Alighiero Boetti

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The Italian artist Boetti made quite a lot of wall hangings using embroidery, chiefly maps of the world, but also tapestry panels showing the letters of the alphabet.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: His interests were naming, writing and maps.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He often made work using embroidery and tapestry, as well as the equally time consuming method of using a ballpoint pen to colour large areas.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Boetti made a series of drawings in ballpoint pen of invisible words.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Reading from a key to the drawing along the top and sides, it is possible to discern words hidden in the drawings by referring to inverted commas on a grid.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The whole paper is coloured by intensive use of the blue or red ballpoint, leaving only the inverted commas white.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: On Kawara

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: A Japanese artist who began working in the 1960s, Kawara is known for a number of conceptual projects and endurance works.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: I Met, I Went is a year of postcards written and mailed to friends and acquaintances by Kawara every day for a year.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The work with which Kawara is usually associated is a constantly accumulating series called the Date Paintings, of which he has made one a day since the 1960s.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Each identical 50 cm high painting has the day’s date painted in white numerals on a black canvas.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Michael Craig Martin

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Craig Martin is British American artist born in the 1940s who makes wall paintings depicting ordinary objects – furniture, paperclips, tools, bicycles, lamps, globes and fittings are juxtaposed without reference to relative scale at various angles.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The objects are placed on very brightly coloured grounds painted with matt emulsion paint and outlined in black plastic tape, except for a period in the 1980s when Craig Martin used square sectioned steel rods bent to shape and welded to create the outlines.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The wall paintings may fill a whole gallery or museum, or just one wall.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Craig Martin’s earlier work made in the 1960s and 70s is conceptual.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: His best known work is the Oak Tree, which consists of a glass of water placed on a glass shelf above the viewer’s head and an accompanying framed text which explains to the viewer why the glass of water is an oak tree, by means of a question and answer between the artist and a fictitious interlocutor.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The artist claims that it is by the authority invested in him as an artist that the glass of water is an oak tree, thus this is a work about authorship and subjectivity.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He also made a work with a row of clipboards and plumb lines hung on a wall, a series of boxes with hinged lids placed on the floor, the lids taking progressively larger parts of the box until the lid was more box and the box was more lid.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Sol Le Witt

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: An American conceptual artist who made installation and drawings, Le Witt is best known for his wall drawings made in pencil directly onto the wall which is painted either black or white.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He devised complex geometric patterns of lines – parallel, radiating or on a grid – which are drawn in coloured pencil, forming a barely perceptible drawing which nevertheless has a strong effect on the space and adds glowing areas of colour.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Le Witt also made a number of sculptures based on the grid.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: These are three dimensional grids formed from 30 cm cubes stacked in rows on the floor.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: the whole sprayed with white lacquer.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Each layer has a different formation and may be up to 40 cubes long.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The cubes are not solid, so that the structure has a complex appearance.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Daniel Buren

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Buren painted lozenge shapes on buildings and architectural structures, making site specific works that use the lozenge shapes as a visual intervention to prompt a reconsideration of the scene presented to the viewer, and attempt to alter the reading of the picture plane, treating an environment as if it were no more than a photograph.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The lozenges allude to signage and logos are entirely without function.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Buren's work is as much to do with reconsidering landscape painting as it is do with installation.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Victor Burgin

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: An American artist who made conceptual work from the 1960s onwards with a strong theoretical slant which is evident both in the work and in his writing about art.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: James Lee Byars

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: One of Byars’s sculptures is a clear acrylic case, containing white sand, a white book, and a cream coloured (almost white) snake.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: This work can be recreated anywhere as long as the artist’s instructions are followed: he specifies the white sand, the dimensions of case and book, which must be made by a bookbinder, and that the snake must be as close to white as is available.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Early conceptualism implied a form of resistance to subversion of the cultural norm.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: This gave the work of these artists a political edge until at the end of the twentieth century conceptualism became the norm.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: One artist who is identified with a subversive intention is Beuys, who made conceptual and political art between the 1950s and the 80s.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Joseph Beuys

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Born in early 1930s Beuys is one of the most significant German artists of the second half to the twentieth century.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He was a professor at the Dusseldorf academy for many years, where he had a huge influence on several generations of younger artists.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Beuys was an eccentric character who always dressed in the same canvas hat and black canvas shooting waistcoat with multiple pockets.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He was extremely prolific, working in all media but chiefly known as a sculptor, performance and installation artist who proclaimed that ‘life is art’, thus making his every action a part of his work.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Beuys is notorious for the myth of a near death experience that surrounds him and although long since discredited has proved impossible to ignore.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: It was said that he had been shot down when flying for the Luftwaffe in the second world war over snowy mountains.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: His life was saved by local villagers who found him and kept his body temperature up by smearing him in pig fat and wrapping him in felt.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Whether apocryphal or not, this event would seem to have had a profound influence on most of Beuys’s work, given that his favoured materials are felt and fat.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: However, Beuys’s personal lexicon is often impenetrable and inaccessible.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: One of his best known works is Portrait of the Artist Talking to a Dead Hare, which was made for his first solo show in New York in 1979.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Beuys sat in the gallery, his head covered in honey and gold leaf (also highly important symbolic substances in his work), cradling a dead hare in his arms and talking to it.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: As a declared socialist and an anti capitalist, politics are a major feature of Beuys’s work.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He was sacked from his academic post at Dusseldorf for inciting student riots, although the exact truth is subject to speculation.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: In his second New York show he made a work with a live wolf, titled I Like America and America Likes Me.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Beuys sat in the gallery behind a chain link fence separating him and the viewer, talking to the wolf for a week.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The wolf symbolised the plundering and appropriation of the American wilderness and by his interaction with its spirit Beuys was trying to heal the wounds caused to the indigenous people.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Beuys’s best known work is Fat Chair, a wooden chair with lard piled at a slant towards the back of it.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He made a number of works from stacks of plate steel and felt which he described as batteries, a kind of life preserving power source.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: A number of vitrines containing an array of mysterious but apparently utilitarian metal, wood, fat and felt objects.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: A series of performances given by Beuys took the format of lectures often conducted in a studio, in which he used blackboards to illustrate a talk, usually about the possibility of art being life, and in particular to make his famous claim that ‘Art is a Social Sculpture’.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: By this he meant that art could not exist without the interaction of the viewer, it was therefore subjective, and thus a social event and by extension political.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The blackboards with their drawings, diagrams and writings remain as a document of the lecture.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Beuys made himself a felt suit and various other garments and items, which usually had a cross cut from cotton fabric stitched onto them.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: In 1985 Beuys installed rolls of felt the height of a London gallery all round the walls and across the entrance, leaving only a small three foot high gap from the floor up for the viewer to enter.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Inside was a grand piano.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: A total damped silence was implied by felt and experienced by the deadened acoustic.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Beuys also made a work consisting of a Volkswagen camper van with a number of wooden sledges emerging from its door, linked by a harness.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Public works consisted of the planting of 5000 trees in a small town and the casting of a concrete public underpass by pouring melted lard into it and then cutting it out.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Beuys made many works on paper, using charcoal, paint, ink and, in particular, a specific brand of rust coloured paint, the kind used to preserve sail cloth or paint door steps.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The name of the paint and the colour was personally symbolic.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: In the first half of the century some artists were involved more directly in politics.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.3; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.508

g.text:soa: ART AND POLITICS

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Artists have often used their skills in the service of their political beliefs, sometimes by working as official state artists, in which case they were well provided for.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The Soviet government used socialist realist art as a propaganda tool and so artists who wanted to resist found other ways of working.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Chinese state artists were similarly employed, some even worked at altering photographs to suit the government’s needs.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Artists working under totalitarian regimes who had opposing political beliefs may have had no choice but to serve the state or risk punishment.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: In order to avoid this many defected or worked underground and in these situations art has often been a tool of resistance or subversion.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Most of these artists did not achieve great fame due to the circumstances in which they had to live, but some did.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Picasso’s Guernica is a well known work of political resistance.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Some artists simply used their skills to record what they found abhorrent.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Kathe Kollwitz

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Kollwitz is an Austrian artist who made contemporaneous drawings in the concentration camps during the holocaust mainly in graphite and charcoal often depicting women.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Diego Rivera

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Rivera was a Mexican mural painter working in the 1930s and 40s who made political wall paintings celebrating ordinary people and workers in public buildings in the service of the socialists.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He fell out of favour when the socialist government gave way to a right wing party who found him politically embarrassing and prevented him from finishing his last major public commission.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Rivera was the husband of the artist Frida Kahlo and a friend of Leon Trotsky.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The posters used by the demonstrators in the national strike and demonstrations in Paris and other cities in May 1968 borrowed the ideas of the Situationist International group of artists, who set up a poster printing workshop to make them.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: These bold graphic one colour screen prints had simple images and texts, for example ‘Under the pavement is the Beach’ and ‘Beauty is in the streets’.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.3; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.508

g.text:soa: THE SITUATIONIST INTERNATIONAL

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Guy Debord

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Founder of the Situationist International, a Paris based group of international artists, Debord led the group with his revolutionary ideas (and politics).

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Debord took Baudelaire's idea of the flaneur, the wanderer through a city, and developed it into his personal concept of the ‘dérive’, a directed walk through urban scenery.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Debord believed that people should interact with their city, to which end he had various ideas including putting light switches on street lamps so that the people could turn them on and off at will.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Asger Jorn

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: A Dutch artist and member of the Situationists, Jorn made collages with torn posters, for example a sixteenth century portrait of a woman in a blue brocade dress has her face defaced by the additions of paint and a collaged element.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: There was a strong performative element in what the Situationists proposed.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Many artists in the 70s took conceptual objections to the status of the art object to its logical extreme and began to make performance art, dispensing with the object and any sense of permanence entirely, using their own bodies as both subject and material.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Performance art was also a focus for many women artists who saw it as a way to make work about reclaiming of the female body by women.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.3; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.508

g.text:soa: PERFORMANCE ART

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Carolee Schneeman

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: American artist Schneeman’s best known work is Meatjoy (1975), for which a large number of naked performers were instructed to perform an orgiastic celebration by wallowing in animal entrails and pieces of meat and blood.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: EyeBody was a solo work by Schneeman in which she sat on a swing, naked, in a space with white backdrop paper on the walls, holding an umbrella.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: During the performance she made a drawing by swinging as close as she could to the walls and drawing on them.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: For another work Interior Scroll, Schneeman read out loud a poem that she had written, from a long strip of paper previously inserted into her vagina and gradually extracted as she read.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Schneeman’s Olympia, made in collaboration with sculptor Robert Morris, was a performance in which she posed as the woman in Manet's eponymous painting.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Morris, dressed in a white robe and wearing leather work gloves, carried large plywood boards around, arranging them as a backdrop to Schneeman.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Both performers wore white makeup.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The piece was concerned with the ‘work’ of art, about the male artist and the female model, and about the translation from two to three dimensions, the boards representing ‘planes’.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Tseching Hsieh

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: This Chinese artist made a performance in the early 1980s for which he was tied to another person by a rope 3 metres long for one year.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Allan Kaprow

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Kaprow is best known for his Happenings in New York in the late 1960s.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: These were site specific installations in which a performance would happen witnessed by an invited audience.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The Happenings were one of the earliest examples of artists making live art in galleries or gallery like spaces rather than in a theatre or studio space.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: One Happening took place in a loft in which a structure of stud wall frames covered with transparent plastic sheeting created a box like space in which the performers could be seen but were obscured.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Kaprow wrote a seminal book about the Happenings which was influential for artists making time based work.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Eleanor Antin

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Antin is an American artist best known for her work Carving: a Traditional Sculpture made in 1971, for which she put herself on a strict diet and had a male doctor weigh and measure her every day for a month.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: This is one of a number of works in which Antin investigated the effect of the ideals forced upon women in a patriarchal society.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: In this work she attempted to literally sculpt her own body, making a comment both on women’s control over their own bodies, on the centuries of depiction of the nude female body by men, and on women’s continuing need to make themselves attractive for men.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The performance was documented by one photograph every day that were then placed together in a grid and framed, and by a video.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: During the 1980s Antin began to make more theatrical performances, using cut out puppets.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: She also developed an alter ego, Eleanora Antinova, a trans gender Russian ballet dancer who appeared in a tutu and a long beard.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Marina Abramovic and Ulay

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Abramovic first came to public attention when she invited visitors to a gallery in which she appeared naked, stating that the visitors could do anything they wanted to her and she would not resist or retaliate.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: She provided a number of implements with which to do this including knives and a gun.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Abramovic narrowly avoided serious injury but discovered that her initial premise was correct: like the invisible barrier of etiquette surrounding an artwork, there was a barrier of propriety and embarrassment protecting her that was only broached when the beginnings of a mob mentality formed.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Abramovic worked together with her partner Ulay until the early 1980s making performance ‘sculptures’ and endurance works.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: A work entitled Breathe linked them in a mouth to mouth embrace for as long as they could breathe using their combined exhaled breath.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: They braided their hair together and stayed sitting back to back for eight hours.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: For another work they used a full size bow and arrow and stood facing each other, with Ulay holding the string and Abramovic holding the arrow at the point on the centre of the bow string from which it is released.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: They maintained this state of equilibrium through tension until the strain of holding on meant they had to either stop or let go of the tension in the bow.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: This would have resulted in the release of the arrow, which was aimed at Abramovic.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: In Doorway they stood naked and facing each other on either side of the entrance to the gallery.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: This meant that those wishing to enter were forced to brush past them and had to choose who to face as they turned sideways to enter.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: These partner works focused on endurance through concentration and on the tension in partnerships manifested in physical mutual support.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: They are notable for the degree of politeness and gentleness combined with a power and implicit violence.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The artists described them as sculptures.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: After the relationship with Ulay ended Abramovic continued to make endurance works.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: While these maintained a formal sculptural quality they also acquired a ritual aspect, as in the work in which she sat in a circle of salt surrounded by poisonous snakes.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: In another work created in an amethyst mining town in Brazil, she made and wore clogs from blocks of amethyst.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Abramovic made a work for a tree sited in a public square in which she placed a number of speakers playing birdsongs so that it seemed that the tree was teeming with tiny birds.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Vito Acconci

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Acconci, an American artist, made several endurance works in the early 1970s, notably Seedbed, for which he built a false gallery floor which sloped up from the door to the rear of the space.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Acconci was reputedly sealed in the void under the floor masturbating.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: In another work he constructed a shelf high up on the gallery wall in such a way that he could not be seen by those in the gallery from any angle and stayed on the shelf for the hours during which the gallery was open.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: In these works he made the gallery space and the viewer’s own feelings about being in that space into the subject of the work.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: A smaller scale work involved a video on a monitor placed on a furry rug on the floor.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: On the screen Acconci is seen, lying on his stomach, his face right up against the camera, talking to the viewer and inviting them to lie down on the rug and join him on the floor.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Chris Burden

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Burden became known in the late 1960s and early 70s for his performance work that mostly involved physical endurance.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: In ‘Shoot’ he arranged for a friend to shoot him in the arm in a gallery at a specified time in front of an audience.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The shooting, which did not seriously injure Burden, was documented and like all his works of the period, the documentation became the work.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: In Locker Piece he had himself locked in a left luggage locker at a railway station for eight hours.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: In Freeway he lay in the middle of a freeway.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He also had himself nailed to the bonnet of a Volkswagen Beetle through his hands and feet.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Burden was interested in making formal sculptural work using his own body and in the visual power of pain and danger.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The purity and simplicity of the works made them very powerful.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: In his later work he developed an interest in war and military capability through his pacifist beliefs and interest in ecology and the environment.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He made a work involving hundreds of tiny model submarines, and a large meteorite like lump suspended from the gallery ceiling with model railway track running all over it and in and out of it.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: In 1999 Burden constructed a large and complex computer controlled machine for making and throwing paper aeroplanes.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Joan Jonas

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: An American performance artist and musician who worked with Judson Church dancers Yvonne Rainer and Merce Cunningham, Jonas made a performance work in which she played the cello.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Dara Birnbaum

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Birnbaum is an American artist best known for her performance in which she dressed as Wonder Woman.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Some women artists made work that although not performed was performative in its intention.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: They included Judy Chicago and Mary Kelly.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Judy Chicago

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: American artist Chicago changed her name from the patronymic to that of her birthplace as a feminist gesture in the 1970s.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Chicago’s work The Dinner Party from 1972 became an iconic feminist work.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: It is a narrow table arranged in a triangular format, with place settings for all the famous and unsung heroines of American life, for example Mrs Lincoln.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The place settings are actually embroideries depicting plates, each one made by a different woman artist, similar to the way women make church kneelers.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Chicago wanted to draw attention to the under representation of women’s achievement by staging this imaginary dinner party of these great women, using traditionally female but culturally undervalued materials and methods.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: She brought the women together by means of the dinner table because this is how women had traditionally brought people together.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The work came to be seen as representative of the struggle for recognition of women from all areas of life and times, and was influential for several succeeding generations of artists.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Mary Kelly

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: An American artist who made works dealing with feminist issues from the 1970s onwards.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Kelly’s seminal work is the Post Partum Document, an extremely influential work made in 1973 documenting the birth and emergence into language of her son Kelly.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The work takes the form of about thirty framed panels, each containing an object and a text.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The object might be a soiled nappy (which helped to gather tabloid attention at the time), or an item of clothing.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The text details the child’s weight and length, age in weeks, and describes his development with notes on his linguistic development.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: In this work Kelly documents not only the birth of her child but also her care for his life as a creative activity.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: This startlingly simple and obvious statement caused a great deal of criticism and publicity, and the Post Partum Document was declared not to be art, to be offensive and even cruel.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Despite the criticism Kelly was widely acknowledged to have raised the issue of motherhood as a taboo, as work that is not to be considered work, not on a par with artistic achievement and not to be revealed in all its messy detail.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The work’s form was important.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: It was predominantly a text work and this was another of Kelly’s points – that text, or language, is how the subject is constituted and that we are not subjects until we are speaking subjects.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The emergence of a child into language is therefore the most important moment in our existence.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Kelly drew on the works of Lacan, the French literary theorist who developed the theory of the other and the difference between the male and female subject, and of psychoanalytic writers such as Freud and Klein.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Lacan's theories on the constitution of the subject were particularly influential for a whole generation of artists in the 1980s, mostly but not all of them women.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Kelly’s later work developed into institutional critique and was always wall and text based.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: She made a work that consisted of highly crafted metal medallions or wall plaques.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Hannah Darboven

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Artist working in the 1960s and 70s who made works using text.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Darboven was interested in catalogues, indexes and diaries, one work for example took hundreds of index cards on which the artist had written and displayed them carefully categorised.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The text on the cards however consisted only of ‘x’s.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: This display of an organising system that contained no information served to visualise a practice which is in use in daily life, but which is never actually seen and rarely considered.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Darboven’s obsessive writing projects are always made by hand.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Hannah Wilke

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: American artist who became known in the 1970s for her photographic and performance work.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Wilke often appeared naked, which was controversial at a time when feminist artists were reclaiming the female body, traditionally painted naked by men, for themselves.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: For one performance she appeared naked but wearing high heeled shoes on the steps of a public building.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Wilke’s Chewing Gum Scarification Series is her best known work, in which she applied a large number of ‘scars’ made from chewed gum to her naked torso and photographed herself.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: These scars were also exhibited as sculptures.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Wilke made a video work which shows her in her apartment, mostly on the phone to a man with whom it seems evident she is flirting.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The film is a study in body language and how the viewer interprets it.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Martha Rosler

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: American artist who began her career in the seventies making a number of photographic and text based works which juxtapose text and image to make work that highlights social inequity and challenges assumptions.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: She is best known for her seminal work the Bowery Project.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: This consists of a series of photographs paired with texts that juxtapose words or phrases used to describe people who live on the streets with images of the area in which they live.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: An image of a banking hall doorway, for example, is paired with the phrase ‘down and out’.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: An early collaborative work called Metal Box Factory is a systematic survey of a number of employees in a factory around 1970.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Rosler asked the workers to write down their daily schedules both at work and home, displayed the results and made a comparison of the time spent working and at home.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The schedules reveal the amount of work done in the home mostly by the women to be almost as much as the work done in the factory.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Clocking on cards and production line rotas are also part of the display of material in the installation.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Rosler made a series of collages showing domestic interiors that are (often humorous) comments on the division of labour in the home and the role of the housewife.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Rosler is one to the earliest artists to make politicised feminist work which presented a critique of society.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Performance art often combined video and installation.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Some artists like Bruce Nauman had a multi disciplinary practice.
