text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Bruce Nauman

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Nauman is an American artist who began his career in the 1960s making performance, installation, sculpture and video work.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: In fact Nauman made some of the earliest video art, in the days when the technology was new and only television broadcast equipment was available.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: This was bulky and heavy, and editing equipment was not readily available.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Nauman was also one of the first artists to consider the television monitor as an art object in itself, as seen in his corridor installation.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: This consists of two 4 metre high freestanding white walls, placed next to each other with a gap in between.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The walls are at a slight angle so that the gap between them narrows gradually until it is the width of a monitor, which shows only white interference.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: As the viewer approaches the work from the wider end, the light from the monitor creates a hypnotic effect so that the viewers feel compelled to enter the corridor and walk as far as they can before they no longer fit the space.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: This is intended to represent the tunnel with a white light at the end that is often described by those who have had a near death experience.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: In the 1960s and 70s, Nauman made several performed works that are usually viewed as video documents.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The most well known is Taking a Line for a Walk, in which Nauman is seen walking around a square marked on the floor.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Another work, a development of this piece, is a 4 metre high white box round which the viewer can walk.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: A closed circuit television monitor is placed at each corner, on which the viewer sees himself or herself passing the previous monitor.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The film playing on the monitor is played back at slight delay, so that the viewers are following themselves.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: At the same time, since they are walking around a square, the implication is that they ought to be able to catch up with themselves.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Nauman made other video works, one for example in which he is dressed as a clown and laughs uncontrollably for thirty minutes.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The way the video is presented is always important; in this the monitor is in a wooden cubicle.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: In the 1980s Nauman began to make more static sculptural work, and began a series in which he cast dogs in rubber and displayed them in various ways, for example hanging them from the ceiling in a carousel like structure.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: In the 1990s Nauman made a large scale video installation for which he filmed himself, head and shoulders, talking to himself, and presented a number of these films on 2 metre high flat screen monitors placed upside down.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Cinema and the work of experimental filmmakers had a great influence on many artists and with the advent of early video technology the distinction between art and film became blurred.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Nam June Paik

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: This American artist was one of the first to make and show video as a sculpture.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Paik was also the first artist to broadcast his work on national television, which he did by purchasing advertising slots.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The work most often associated with him is a robot made from television monitors.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: William Wegman

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Wegman is an American artist who made a number of videos in the 1970s featuring himself and his pet dog, a Weimaraner named Fay Wray.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The dog performs a number of actions, such as licking up a line drawn in milk on the studio floor, which Wegman himself also tries to do, considerably less efficiently.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Two similar dogs sit face on to the camera following something off screen intently in perfect unison, the object of the dogs’ attention moving sometimes slowly and sometimes dramatically and violently.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The videos are filmed in black and white in a single shot with no editing.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Wegman went on to make colour photographs of the dog dressed in clothes.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.3; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.508

g.text:soa: EXPERIMENTAL FILM

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Kenneth Anger

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: An underground filmmaker born in the 1950s whose best known film Scorpio Rising had an influence on a whole generation of artists and filmmakers.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: A number of artists made site specific work that, like performance art, relied on photographic documentation for its dissemination and permanence.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: This became known as land art.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.3; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.508

g.text:soa: LAND ART

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Dennis Oppenheim

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Much of Oppenheim's work was site specific land art with a performative endurance element.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: For one of Oppenheim’s best known works, Trench, he suspended his outstretched body by pressing with his hands and feet against the top of two opposite walls of a purpose built trench.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: For another he lay in the sun until his skin was burnt and had changed colour, calling his sunburn the evidence that an artwork had been made.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Robert Smithson

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Smithson's work is nearly always site specific and involves him altering the natural environment, either by rearranging it or by placing mirrors so that the landscape reflects itself.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He is interested in the perspective of the map in terms of making the ground his work surface or picture plane, and in creating ‘images’ which, like the topography represented by a map, are only visible from the air.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: In one sense, then, his work is intentionally invisible.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Smithson’s use of mirrors is a development of this interest in making formal rearrangements of the natural world.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The mirror works occupied a variety of locations, including rural ones and one in Manhattan in which large mirrors are stood on the ground at specific angles.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Spiral Jetty is the best known work by any land artist.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: It was made by taking several tonnes of small rock to a salt lake and building a walkway, which leaves the beach and follows a very large spiral that is only visible form the air.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Spiral Jetty has over the years been submerged by the lake and now ceases to exist.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: However, it was documented in photographs and on film, like all of Smithson’s work, and this is the form in which his work is most commonly experienced.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: In fact Smithson was very interested in the dichotomy between the reality of his work experienced in situ and in a photograph (which shows the work in an entirely different way).

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He made a number of other earthworks and plans for earthworks, and also made work using maps.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Mary Miss

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: American artist born in the late 1940s who made a number of earthwork sculptures, for example a cube shaped void sunk into the ground which had its top exactly level with the surface, and could be entered on ramps from ground level.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Miss subverted minimal sculptural forms being made by her contemporaries by making them absolutely concrete but invisible.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Agnes Denes

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The American artist Denes planted and cultivated a field of wheat in Manhattan on a two acre landfill site in 1982.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Denes wanted to make a work about world trade, the economics of food production and famine.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Walter De Maria

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Known for his permanent installation Lightning Field of 1987 which is a site in Arizona, in a specific area that has the highest frequency of lightning strikes in the world.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: De Maria set out a square mile of lightning conductor poles linked by conductive wires which when struck by lightening animate the field in a spectacle of blue light and electrical activity.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.3; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.508

g.text:soa: SITE SPECIFIC ART

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Gordon Matta Clark

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: American artist Matta Clark is best known for his work House, a suburban clapboard house that the artist cut in two vertically down the centre.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The two halves lean outwards and away from each other.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Matta Clark made a number of other works which involved cutting through buildings, for example a project at the opening of the Pompidou Centre in Paris in which he cut several circular and elliptical holes through a nearby building that was about to be redeveloped.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Although major in terms of their execution, Matta Clark’s interventions are visually extremely simple.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Christo and Jeanne Claude

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Beginning in the 1970s French artist Christo and his partner Jeanne Claude began wrapping objects, to transform one thing into another, solidify forms, change a hard form to an apparently soft one, graduating to larger and larger objects.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: They began to work with fabric on a large scale, either wrapping buildings or the landscape.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: They used parachute silk, vinyl and other kinds of industrial fabric with the required properties.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Several works exemplify what they do best.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: For example, Valley Curtain, made in the early 1980s, was a large orange curtain hung across a valley somewhere in California.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Running Fence is a mile long fence of red fabric that follows the contours of a hill.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The artists installed a large number of table umbrellas dotted over a hillside.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The Island Skirts surround a number of small islands, following the shoreline and floating on the water for thirty metres or so.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: As with all their work, the proportions of the intervention always take the view from a distance into account.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The work is by its nature temporary and is always made with the final photographic document in mind.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Thus the island skirts were designed to be wide enough to be clearly visible in an aerial photograph, and the locations are very carefully chosen with the final photograph in mind.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: In the 1990s Christo and Jeanne Claude completed their most ambitious projects, the Wrapped Reichstag and the Wrapped Pont Neuf.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: These structures were wrapped in a fabric that was light enough to fold and gather around the forms they covered, and bound with rope.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The Pont Neuf was wrapped in a gold fabric resulting in a transformation that was a triumph of planning, negotiation and construction.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: There are still postcards of the work on every Parisian postcard rack.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.3; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.508

g.text:soa: FIGURATIVE PAINTING

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: In Britain in the early twentieth century many figurative painters were engaged in a gritty realism that echoed the post war reality.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Stanley Spencer

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: British artist Spencer painted English rural life and religious subjects, often combining the two.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He often showed god or Jesus in a scene set in an English village.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The paintings are sometimes large and the composition is crowded.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Spencer’s figures are often solidly built with heavy limbs, almost statue like, and he kept to a palette of grey, brown and ochre.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Ivon Hitchens

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Hitchens’s English landscapes with vegetation and flowers are painted with loose flowing brushstrokes leaving parts of the canvas unpainted.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He favoured subdued earth colours, purples, blues and greens.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: John Bratby

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Bratby was one of a group known as the kitchen sink painters for their choice of domestic subject matter.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Bratby's interiors showed his own home and family, painted with thickly encrusted paint often squeezed directly from the tube and applied with a palette knife, in an almost naïve style.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Cecil Collins

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: British twentieth century visionary painter.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: LS Lowry

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: British artist Lowry lived and worked in the North of England and painted scenes of everyday and working class life in the cities of the North.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He became known as a kind of people’s painter, a painter of ‘matchstick men and matchstick cats and dogs’ immortalised in a popular music song.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Lowry’s paintings showed the grey light of northern winters and the relentless coming and going of daily life, with buildings and a multitude of tiny people walking past.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The people are painted in two or three brushstrokes, suggestions of figures so that Lowry could paint a great number of them on one painting.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The paintings are often predominantly grey or white, the figures in dark colours with little hints of brighter colours.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Lucian Freud

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: A British figurative painter who was born in the 1930s, Freud began his career precociously in his teens and was still painting in 2003.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He paints portraits, usually of models, sometimes of friends, family, and sometimes of well known people, although he rarely accepts commissions.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: His models are almost always nude, or semi clothed and painted in accurate detail, but with a psychological perspective.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: They are often lying down.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The predominant colours of the paintings are consistent: skin tones, and the greys and browns of his studio are the background to all his works since he never paints anywhere else.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: A painting may take up to twenty or so sittings, and some sitters are not able to continue.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He has often painted a favourite model repeatedly.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Some of Freud’s paintings might be of two people lying together, or there may be a dog, often a greyhound.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He favours gaunt loose skinned physiques but has also painted larger people.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Freud’s subjects include himself, his lovers, his models (sometimes the two are the same), his daughters, artist Leigh Bowery, the Queen of England and the fashion model Kate Moss.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Francis Bacon

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Bacon was a very important British painter whose paintings are conceptual but theatrical figurative works with abstract qualities.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: They are nearly always portraits in which the figure is distorted, often to grotesque effect, perhaps looking as if they have been melted or brushed away, appearing to be in discomfort.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The figures are rendered with rough brushstrokes, and are placed on a contrasting flat colour background, often within a delineated three dimensional space.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Bacon made many self portraits.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: One of his best known works is the diptych Three Screaming Popes; three large canvases each with a portrait of a pope in a cope and mitre, within a kind of abstract geometric frame structure, on dark orange and red grounds.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The faces of the popes are blurred and distorted.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He also painted a dog that is either curled up or chasing its tail.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: As with Bacon’s other work, there is an impression of movement, as if a photograph has been taken on a long exposure and the sitter moved, leaving a trail of the movement on the image.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Bacon was almost as well known for his lifestyle as for his work.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: A heavy drinking habitué of bars in Soho in London he lived a solitary and obsessive working life, rarely spending a day without painting.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: His studio was famously untidy and dirty.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Bacon died in the 1990s.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Painting had begun to aspire to the condition of photography, particularly in America.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: This was to become a major theme in the work of Richter and others later on, but initially there were only a few interested artists.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Photorealist painters literally mimicked the appearance of a photograph.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Chuck Close

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Close initially made photo realist paintings but he is best known for his gridded paintings which, although they pre date digital technology, have the appearance of pixilated images.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Inspired by the printing process and the way an image is broken down into dots of three colours, Close developed a way of placing a grid of squares of about 3 by 3 cm over the image he wanted to paint, very often a self portrait.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He then produced the image by painting each square a different colour so that from a distance the image would be readable but close up the coloured squares would be predominate.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: In doing so he was investigating both the effect of photographic printing and painting, making a painting that looked photographic, as painting had been trying to do, yet not in the conventional sense.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: All this work was made before the digital revolution that has made Close’s paintings look exactly like pixels.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: As well as paintings, Close also made works on paper in watercolours.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He made a series of self portraits using black and greys that emulate black and white photos.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Reinhardt Voight

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: An American artist born around 1950, Voight makes paintings based on a grid.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: In Voight’s early work he translated a photographic image into a coloured grid, degrading the image almost entirely, an idea that prefigured pixellation by decades.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: David Hockney

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: One of the best known of all British twentieth century artists, Hockney was born in the 1940s and began his career in the 1960s, becoming successful while he was still at college.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: At this early stage he often added text to his paintings as in a work titled We Two Boys Together Swinging, where he added the title of the painting in white letters.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Hockney’s most famous painting is called The Bigger Splash.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: It shows an empty swimming pool and diving board with a villa in the background.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The pool is rendered in flat aquamarine and there is a white splash in the water as if someone had just dived in.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: This is the best known representation of a splash in the history of painting.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Hockney went to live in Los Angeles and the swimming pool became his favourite subject.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He became very good at painting water and also painted in watercolour on tiled sheets of watercolour paper.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He continued to paint in watercolour in 2003, making large scale full length portraits.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Drawings constitute a major part of Hockney’s oeuvre.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He used a single confident line, pencil or pen, and also made a number of lithographs and etchings.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: His drawings are restrained and monochrome in comparison to his often bright paintings.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He drew his friends and lovers incessantly, and his mother, as well as still lifes, flowers, landscapes and animals, in particular cats and dogs.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: In fact Hockney’s work is extremely traditional in terms of his subject matter, it was rather his means of execution that attracted attention.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Another well known painting by Hockney is Mrs and Mrs Clarke at Home, a double portrait of Ossie and Celia Clarke, fashion designer friends of Hockney’s, seated on opposite sides of a bay window in their London home with their cat next to them.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Hockney also designed a number of stage productions for opera companies, notably the Magic Flute and The Rake’s Progress, painting backdrops as well as designing costumes.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Edward Hopper

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: An American artist who began his career in the 1940s, Hopper is one of the most popular painters of American life, mostly but not always choosing urban scenes.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He was particularly good at painting night scenes.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: One painting shows a bar at night, a long and low corner building, green on the outside with mostly black on the canvas, but glowing with bright yellow light from its interior.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Inside is a woman waitress and a few solitary male customers.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Another painting shows a petrol station at night, another a person on a lonely road at by a payphone, caught in the headlights of an oncoming car.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Hopper depicted the melancholy and loneliness that he found in modern life.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Norman Rockwell

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: American artist who made paintings that represented the American way of life, and who became synonymous with a certain idealised view of America.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Rockwell painted rural scenes depicting life on farmsteads, domestic interiors, fireside scenes and landscapes.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: A particularly well known work is a painting of a meadow filled with poppies in which a little girl is sitting.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Rockwell painted in a highly realistic illustrative style avoiding any reference to painting as object.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He spent his career making an impeccably painted record of America between the 1940s and 60s, many of which were printed on the cover of Picture Post and became images that entered into the national consciousness.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Georgia O’Keefe

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: O’Keefe is well known for her paintings of hugely enlarged flowers in very strong colours which also allude to the female anatomy.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: O’Keefe spent many years living in the desert in New Mexico from which she derived much of her inspiration, also making a series of works depicting bleached animal bones and skulls which she found there.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Through her flower paintings O’Keefe succeeded in turning a traditionally delicate subject into large bold and even aggressive or threatening forms.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Frida Kahlo

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: This Mexican artist was born in the 1920s and made figurative paintings, largely self portraits.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Kahlo depicted the tragedy of her life in her paintings, which are graphic and detailed.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: She shows herself in many guises, with her distinguishing eyebrows that meet in the middle, and her long braided hair and native Mexican dress.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: She details her gynaecological problems and back problems stemming from a trolley bus accident as a young girl (which eventually took her life prematurely in the 1950s) in her paintings, in particular a number of miscarriages (she shows the foetus outside her womb, still attached by the umbilical cord, for example) and the restraining corset which she wore to support her spine in her last years.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Kahlo's discomfort and anger at her body’s inability to fulfil its biological destiny, coupled with a feminist fury at the obstacles faced by a woman trying to succeed as a serious painter at that time, also fed into her work.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Kahlo’s paintings are disturbing and often horrific but also full of bright colours and pattern.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Kahlo lived with the Mexican muralist Diego Rivera for part of her life.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Philip Guston

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: American Guston made abstract expressionist work at the beginning of his career in the 1950s and early 60s.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He then had a crisis of belief in abstraction and began to paint figuratively.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Guston developed a distinctive personal iconography that included cigarette butts, ashtrays, horseshoes, shoes, and Klu Klux Klansmen’s pointed hats, painted in a cartoon like style with heavy black outlines.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The objects in particular can be seen as self portraits.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Paintings include a pile of shoes, old and battered boots with the odd horseshoe, an ashtray overflowing with giant, very fat cigarette butts, and a series of paintings of figures wearing Klansmen’s hats in which the figures are often facing each other as if trying to converse.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Guston typically used either a monochrome palette of grey, brown, black and white (for example in the painting of a pile of horseshoes), or a bright palette.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: His bright colours are blue, red and a fairly bright light pink, the pink often used as a background.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Some of the Klansmen paintings are black on white.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Guston depicts a lonely world, yet not without a bleak humour, spending long hours in the studio smoking and trying to communicate with the rest of the world.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Sam Fernandez

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: American artist Fernandez made psychedelic paintings in the 1960s and 70s, which were sometimes used for record covers.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: They consist of a richly dense backgrounds of patterns and flowers flowing into the main element of the image.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Fernandez’s work influenced graphic design and was re discovered in the 1990s by a new generation of artists.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Nancy Spero

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Spero’s narrative paintings include small figures.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: She also made a work called A Tribute to Anna Mendieta (the wife of artist Carl Andre who died when she fell from the 30th floor of a building, reputedly pushed by Andre).

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: This work is a pair of red handprints at the top of the gallery wall, which are dragged in a red smear down the wall as if someone with bloody hands was trying to hold on.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Helmut Newton

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Although not a painter, German photographer Newton was very influential among artists.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He made black and white or occasionally coloured photographs of women, naked or clothed, but always objectified as glamorous, made up and fashionable.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Newton always photographed his models wearing very high heels.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Newton’s images fell out of favour for a time in the 1970s when feminist critics claimed back the female form, but he continued to make work.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Newton’s women often seemed like objects for male pleasure but in fact they have a strange autonomy, despite their nakedness.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Sometimes several women might be photographed together as in a well known image of several models standing in a group staring at the camera.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.3; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.508

g.text:soa: EARLY TWENTIETH CENTURY SCULPTURE

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Henry Moore

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Moore, a British artist born at the beginning of the twentieth century, began as a figurative sculptor, but later became a pioneer of semi abstract sculptural form in Britain, and made many public commissions.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Like his peer Barbara Hepworth, Moore’s sculptures often have holes through them and hollows; he too was interested in representing the ‘void’ sculpturally.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He worked in stone, bronze and clay.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Unlike his contemporaries, however, Moore did not make smooth surfaced works; his roughly modelled sculptures are like giant bones, and always refer clearly to the human form.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: For example a reclining nude (a favourite form for Moore) might be abstracted from a series of voids and hollows, as if it were a piece of driftwood that had been worn away.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: A standing figure might have a large space where the belly would have been.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Heads are featureless and the proportions of the body adjusted to suit the form that Moore was trying to achieve.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Moore’s sculptures are often sited in rural landscapes and parks, and indeed it was the way in which the human form could be made to look as if it were part of the landscape that interested Moore.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: A late example of this is an arch (around 1960) made for a lakeside site in Hyde Park in London which seems to be constructed of three monumental bones, two standing on their ends, the other balancing across the two.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Moore made a large number of drawings, both as preparatory sketches and in their own right.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: His drawings are realistic and anatomically accurate, as shown in a series of studies of hands.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: As well as drawing the figure, he made a series of impressions of people sheltering from bombs in an underground station during World War Two.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Jacob Epstein

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: A British sculptor whose best known work is Rock Drill, the head and torso of a futuristic automaton like creature with a head shaped like an animal skull.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The breastplate ribcage is carved with angular geometric lines and the head is turned to one side.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Some of Epstein’s work reflects the agony of war.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Epstein worked mostly in stone although he did make some bronze casts.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Jacob and the Angel is a massive male and female figure both with huge thick limbs embracing each other.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: It is carved from a tan coloured but translucent stone.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Epstein made a similar carving of a prone figure, a little like an Egyptian mummy.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Elisabeth Frink

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: British artist born in the 1930s who has made bronze heads, busts and equestrian statues from the 1960s onwards.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Frink is particularly known for her distinctive thin figures riding horses bareback whose tiny heads have strangely flat features.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The surface of the sculptures is usually roughly modelled.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Frink’s work can be seen in many public sites in London.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Niki De St Phalle

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: French artist who makes large and small (ranging from table sized to outdoor public sculptures) papier mâché and fibreglass sculptures of human and animal forms.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: These are somewhat like totem poles or other tribal art objects, being mainly highly stylised white smoothed forms that are richly decorated with hand painted patterns particularly on the head and limbs.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Louise Bourgeois

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Bourgeois is an American sculptor born in the 1920s.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: She has had one of the longest careers of any female artists of her generation.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Bourgeois has made works that are both intimate and monumental in scale, and all her work has a strong female sensibility.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: She has made, carved and cast sculpture and installations.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Notable are her carved marble works of the 1950s and 60s, they are often quite small organic curvy shapes suggestive of the inside of the body or of plant growth.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: One of these is made in pink marble set on a plinth.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Installations include room structures that have furniture and objects in them.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Most recently she has made a monumental 30 metre high bronze spider.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Bourgeois repeatedly uses the same motifs such as the shoe and the spider.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Barry Flanagan

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: A British sculptor who mainly made semi abstract stone sculptures until the 1980s when he began to make figurative work and took the hare as his motif.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Flanagan achieved great success with a series of sculptures featuring the figure of a leaping hare roughly modelled in clay, its legs exaggerated in length, cast in bronze, often painted in ultramarine, set upon a plinth made of a crisscrossed rectangle of lengths of planed wood.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: This hare and plinth combination was repeated in many different materials.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Ed Keinholz

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Keinholz created several installations including the Beanery, a tiny kiosk set up as a bar that the viewer could enter to experience the disorienting scale of the space inside it.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Keinholz's installations usually featured life size figures cast from plaster, unpainted with real furniture, fittings and fabric.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Duane Hanson

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: An American artist who began making his very well known life casts of people in the 1970s.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Hanson’s fibreglass casts of himself and others are the sculptural equivalent of photo realist paintings.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The casts are painted, have real hair added and are dressed to look as if they are real, prompting a double take by the viewer.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Hanson chose very ordinary subjects, for example a police officer, a museum attendant, a pair of overweight and badly dressed American tourists, a motorbike accident victim prostrate with his bike, and a cleaning woman.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Allen Jones

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Jones is a British artist who achieved notoriety in the 1960s and 70s for his sculptures of women as furniture.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Feminists in particular found his work hard to accept and although his work declined in popularity during the 1980s the images of some of his sculptures are known all over the world.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Jones’s sculptures are made by modelling idealised life size female figures.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: These are cast in fibreglass, spray painted realistically and dressed in clothes, usually underwear.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: A characteristic work is a coffee table – a glass top is placed on the back of a kneeling woman who is wearing a basque, stockings and suspenders and extremely high heels.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Other furniture includes a similar table top placed on the shins of a woman lying on her back with her legs bent at hip and knee, shins parallel to the floor and bound with cords to form a ‘z’ shaped support and a stool (a woman crouched over and bound with a specially made upholstered leather seat strapped on to her back, for example).

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Jones also made paintings.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Daniel Spoerri

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Italian sculptor who was part of the Arte Povera movement in the late 1960s and early 1970s.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Spoerri is best known for his upside down table wall piece, a table top strewn with the remains of a meal – wine glass with dregs, dirty plate and brimming ashtray all fixed to the table and defying gravity.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Joseph Cornell

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: An American artist known for making work in boxes.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Cornell’s boxes vary in size and materials, they sometimes have doors, or interior shelves or sections, are often painted, covered in fabric or leather, and contain found items and printed material.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: They are like three dimensional collages.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Abstract sculptors found a wide range of new materials and working methods, expanding the definition of sculpture.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Lynda Benglis

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: An American sculptor working in the 1970s, Benglis made sculptures from brightly coloured polyurethane foam, poured onto the floor and allowed to expand and cohere.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Lee Bonteco

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Bontecou’s wall based constructions made from metal, acrylic sheet, perspex and rivets have the appearance of flowers but due to their materials they also reference aircraft fuselages.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Eva Hesse

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Hesse was born in the 1940s and died in 1969 but her prodigious output is now seen as an important counterpoint to the new and radical minimal sculpture being made at the time, and as also as a turning point for women artists who were in the minority, particularly in this field.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Hesse combined current sculptural preoccupations with unorthodox and traditionally feminine materials and methods.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Her achievement was recognised very early and she was included in several seminal exhibitions including one curated by Lucy Lippard, defining the new work.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Hesse began her career around 1960 as a painter, training under Joseph Albers.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: She made figurative paintings and self portraits, gradually turning to abstraction, until she had a crisis of confidence in her ability to paint.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Hesse ceased to make work until she and her husband travelled to Dusseldorf where a German industrialist collector had offered them a studio residency in a disused factory that he owned.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: There she found an abundance of materials and machine parts lying around, and she began to draw these parts and experiment.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Working in the factory Hesse produced a number of odd abstract drawings based on the machine parts.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: She began to make wall based three dimensional paintings, modelling the surface of the work and adding string following the shapes, as well as projecting elements, the whole of which she painted.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Then she went on to make sculptures with the materials she found on the factory floor.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Her first successful ones were cubes of steel mesh sheets, open on one side.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Hesse pushed equal lengths of rubber tubing through the holes in the mesh in the manner of rug tufting, to create a furry effect on the interior of the box.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: This painstaking task produced two sculptures (one with black tubing, one with transparent tubing), which combined the (traditionally female) techniques of handicraft with those (traditionally male) of industrial fabrication used to make minimal sculpture.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Hesse continued to make wall reliefs from modelling materials, string and paint including Rosy, a breast like form on a buff coloured round with a spiral of string painted in graduated shades from pink to red.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Hesse’s interest in concentric circles was worked in these reliefs and in her Dot graph paper drawings, delicate pencil or pen drawings in which rectangles are filled with row of tiny small circles or rows of concentric circles coloured in with pencil.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The string forms resulted in a wall work consisting of a row of about 25 hemispheres 30 cm in diameter covered with string spiralling round, placed in a horizontal line on a long strip about 40 cm wide, at picture height on the wall.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: From the centre of each hemisphere, cords project and extend to the floor where the ends lie.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The whole piece is painted grey.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Hang up (1967) is a seminal work by Hesse consisting of a two metre by one and a half metre empty frame on the wall, bound with cloth bandage and painted light grey.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: A heavy gauge wire loop projects outwards from the frame that is also wrapped with cloth bandage.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The loop is attached on the bottom right and top left corners and looping out about two metres from the wall and back again.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The viewer may stand inside the loop, in which case they seem to be lassoed by the work.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: This work is an abstract but concrete representation of the nature of looking at paintings.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: String was one of Hesse's favoured materials along with latex and fibreglass.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: She made a string mesh consisting of lengths of cord dipped in latex and strung from the ceiling to form an abject enlarged untidy web.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: She took net shopping bags and stuffed them with scrunched up plastic sheeting, hanging them in clusters, which are strangely anthropomorphic, on the wall.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: She photographed herself lying on a bed covered with a mass of string like spaghetti.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Hesse also used rubber tubing that she filled with plaster to create sausage like forms.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Her work often made allusions to the male and the female body.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The preoccupation with tubular forms and repetition characterises Hesse’s later works, Accession and Accretion.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Accession consists of two 50 cm square black panels mounted on the wall with a space between them filled with a mass of silver wires.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Accretion is a row of one and a half m long fibreglass tubes, slightly crumpled, leaning against the wall placed at regular intervals.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Similar works are a casual arrangement of caved in fibreglass cylinders about 70 cm high and 50 cm wide standing on their ends on the floor, and rows of latex spheres on a sheet.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Dan Flavin

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: An American artist working in the 1970s and 80s, Flavin used fluorescent tubes and the coloured light they produce as his medium.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He created sculptures by leaning the tubes against the wall, sometimes two or three, sometimes a whole row, sometimes placed casually at different angles, sometimes measured and at the same angle.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Some tubes might be placed flat on the floor.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The transformers and cables are very visible and are part of the work.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Example of works are a cruciform formation of cold blue coloured tubes mounted on the wall and three tubes, one red, one blue and one green.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Maya Lin
